clue.text: Hard to control a child, perhaps, after work, hollowed out

indicators.note: the child piece is placed after the work piece
a word hollowed out loses its inside, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: a ward is a child under a guardian's care, one example of a child

explanation.surface: A parent laments that a child is hard to manage after a hollowing day at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awkward is clumsy and difficult to handle or manage.

clue.text: A page in old hat getting changed

indicators.note: the page letter is put inside the old hat piece

parts.note: old hat means out of date, dated

explanation.surface: A page in an antique hat being altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Adapted means modified to suit new conditions, so changed.

clue.text: One who criticises that gets hammered before opening?

definitions.meaning: a carping critic who runs things down
a door's metal striker is banged before the door is opened

explanation.surface: A critic who gets a battering before an opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: A knocker is both a habitual critic and the hinged striker on a front door.

clue.text: Atmosphere from a group of travellers

parts.note: the Roma are a traditionally travelling people

explanation.surface: The mood that comes from a band of travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aroma is a distinctive smell or air, so an atmosphere about something.

clue.text: I diet, pass out and fade away

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A dieter fainting and wasting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' reads as fainting, but 'out' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissipate is to disperse or vanish, so fade away.

clue.text: David Cameron about to steal from the French? That's a worry

indicators.note: the Prime Minister's letters go around the stealing piece

parts.note: David Cameron was British Prime Minister, abbreviated PM
to steal is to rob
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A former prime minister pilfering from France would be a diplomatic headache.
explanation.walkthrough: PM (Prime Minister, as David Cameron was from 2010 to 2016) is placed about ROB and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem is a source of trouble or concern, a synonym for a worry.

clue.text: Father's flat note

parts.note: a pad is a flat, a place to live
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Dad's apartment, or a musical note gone flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain addressed as Father, especially in the forces.

clue.text: Topple across woollen wrap

parts.note: over can mean across, as in over the road
a throw is a blanket or shawl

explanation.surface: Knocking down a shawl thrown across.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow is to bring down or topple a ruler or regime.

clue.text: Student thinner when eating right

indicators.note: the thinner piece takes the right letter inside it

parts.note: leaner means thinner

explanation.surface: A student who slims down when dieting properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject, so a student.

clue.text: Strange end in religious service? Nonsense

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the service piece

parts.note: Mass is a Catholic religious service

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the next word are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd conclusion to a church service seems absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' makes DNE from END, placed in MASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness can mean folly or absurdity, in the sense of nonsense.

clue.text: Loving a short time hugging soldiers (American)

indicators.note: the short time piece wraps around the soldiers piece

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
US abbreviates United States, so American

explanation.surface: A brief embrace among American troops suggests affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means showing romantic or sexual love, a synonym for loving.

clue.text: Peter out with tough conservative

parts.note: to peter out is to fade and die
tough means hard

explanation.surface: Someone fading away alongside a tough traditionalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A diehard is a stubborn traditionalist resisting change, so a conservative in the broad sense.

clue.text: Go for a walk and get lost

definitions.meaning: literally, to set off on a long walk in the country
idiomatically, a rude dismissal telling someone to go away

explanation.surface: Head out walking and lose your way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means hiking, and idiomatically it is a brusque command to go away.

clue.text: Team missing one member, heads of state extremely agitated

parts.note: a team of eleven, such as a cricket or football side, less one player leaves ten

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A side down to ten players, its leaders in a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means nervous and strained, close to agitated.

clue.text: Horrible about good, slow piece of music

indicators.note: the horrible piece goes around the good piece

parts.note: dire means dreadful, horrible

explanation.surface: A judgement that something bad and good is a ponderous tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful, slow song of lament, as at a funeral.

clue.text: Help! Cut with axe! Upset when hospital leaves excuse

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged
the hospital letter leaves the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A frantic cry while being attacked with an axe.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool HELPCUTAXE, 'when hospital leaves' removes H, and 'Upset' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To exculpate is to clear of blame, so to excuse or exonerate.

clue.text: Bar's grime — possibly an ash-grey, strong-scented substance

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: The grimy deposit on a pub bar is perhaps some smelly grey stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of the possessive is part of the fodder: BARSGRIME has nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy grey secretion from sperm whales, prized in perfumery for its scent.

clue.text: Arrogant tailor: he'd be glad, I being short of length

indicators.note: to tailor is to alter, so the letters are reworked
being short of means the length letter is missing from the pool

explanation.surface: A conceited tailor declaring his pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like a noun; it is the anagram signal on HEDBEGLADI less L.
explanation.definitionFit: Big-headed means conceited, too full of oneself, so arrogant.

clue.text: Suppress urge for food

parts.note: to scotch a rumour is to suppress it
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: Fighting off a craving for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a British snack: a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs, then fried.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a picnic and pub dish, so simply an example of food.

clue.text: Lieutenant in clear retreat

indicators.note: the officer goes inside the clear piece

parts.note: sheer means clear, transparent, as of fabric

explanation.surface: An officer in an obvious withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a refuge, a retreat in the sense of a safe place.

clue.text: Cut, touching blooming exposed edge of rock

parts.note: flowers are out when blooming
to crop is to cut

explanation.surface: Pruning near flowers on a bare rock edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' just says the two pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is part of a rock formation visible above the ground surface.

clue.text: Shrew, rat, hamster coming together in anger

indicators.note: the words joined up across their gaps show a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Three small creatures meeting in a fury, a squabbling pet shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is intense fury, a literary synonym for anger.

clue.text: Drink, holding weapon? Penny gets worried

indicators.note: the drink piece holds the weapon piece inside

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
D is the old British abbreviation for a penny, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A drinker holding a gun makes Penny anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed means frightened or anxious, close to worried.

clue.text: Writer's tired and gaunt

definitions.meaning: H. Rider ..., author of King Solomon's Mines

explanation.surface: An author is weary and thin.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's surname is also the adjective for a drawn, exhausted look.

clue.text: Praise former lover returning fortune

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: returning means the fortune word is read backwards

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: Speaking well of an old flame whose luck has come back.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Journalists and friends, maybe they try to get you on board

definitions.text: they try to get you on board

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively
a gang can be a group of friends

explanation.surface: Reporters and their mates hoping to recruit you.
explanation.walkthrough: A press gang forcibly enlisted men into the navy; 'on board' is literal, a ship, not agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang was a band of men who seized recruits for naval ships.

clue.text: Yearn over small underwear

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: to pant for something is to yearn for it

explanation.surface: Longing for small knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pants are underpants in British usage, so underwear.

clue.text: Very stuck in one crack

indicators.note: the very letter is stuck inside the one piece

parts.note: sole means one, only

explanation.surface: Something wedged firmly in a fissure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' is a verb here: to crack a code is to solve it.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a problem or code is to work it out.

clue.text: Teach about the Queen's country

indicators.note: the teaching piece goes around the queen piece

parts.note: to train is to teach
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Tutoring someone on the monarch's realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Country in the sense of land or landscape, as in hill country, means terrain.

clue.text: Catch-22 novel after cover's turned over

indicators.note: turned over means the cover word is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover; the 's is short for is
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: Talk of a famous novel and its flipped jacket, Catch-22 being Joseph Heller's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch-22' looks like the book title, but it is the definition; 'after' is a link meaning the novel follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catch-22 is a no-win situation with contradictory conditions, a dilemma.

clue.text: Put a stop to religious education by force

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
to press is to force

explanation.surface: Ending faith lessons by coercion.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to suppress or restrain, so to put a stop to something.

clue.text: Was afraid of editor after report initially coming in late

indicators.note: the editor piece follows the rest
the first letter of report enters the late piece

parts.note: the late means dead, deceased

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A journalist fearing the editor after a report arrives late.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreaded is the past tense of dread, to fear something greatly.
